SUBJECT:  Election of Officers of the Public Safety Commission

BACKGROUND
Per the Municipal Code, at the first meeting after the beginning of the terms of offices of
its members, the Public Safety Commission is to select its officers, Chairperson and Vice
Chairperson. The Chairperson shall not be elected for more than two (2) consecutive
one (1) year terms. The Chairperson shall preside over all meetings of the Commission.
The Vice Chairperson shall preside over Commission meetings in the absence of the
Chairperson.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the members of the Public Safety Commission per Municipal Code
2-2.408 nominate and elect a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson.

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Overview of CERT Program and Discussion of Trainings

BACKGROUND
The Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) Program was first developed by
the Los Angeles Fire Department in 1985, and the first CERT Team completed its training
in early 1986. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) now uses the
program as the national model for other communities. In June 2003, the Los Angeles
County Fire Department implemented its first department-wide CERT Training program.

In 2022, the Los Angeles County Fire Department reorganized the way they conduct
CERT training courses. As CERT is a national model, the course has steered away from
individual CERT programs for each municipal jurisdiction and instead is offered with a
regional approach where CERT certified individuals can be called upon by Los Angeles
County Fire for any emergency, in any jurisdiction they serve in the region.

ANALYSIS
In major disasters, traditional fire and rescue resources might be overwhelmed, making
immediate response to all those in need challenging. In such situations, it becomes
essential for neighbors to assist each other. The CERT program equips residents with the
skills needed to provide this crucial support.

The Los Angeles County Fire Department provides a free, FEMA-approved 20-hour
CERT training. Conducted by skilled emergency personnel, including firefighters and
EMS staff, the program educates residents on local hazards and essential disaster
response skills like fire safety, light search and rescue, team organization, and disaster
medical operations. Graduates of the program are equipped to assist in their
neighborhoods or workplaces during emergencies when professional responders are not
immediately available. Participation in CERT is voluntary, with no obligation for trained
individuals to act during a disaster.
   ITEM 4

The next upcoming regional training is being held in Pico Rivera next month. The City is
also working with other local cities to provide additional trainings in calendar year 2024
and will provide updates once those trainings are set.

Upcoming Training Details:
Hybrid CERT Training – Pico Rivera
Dates: February 10 and 17, 2024
Time: February 10 (9 A.M. - 5 P.M.), February 17 (9 A.M. - 1 P.M.)
Location: Pico Park, 9528 Beverly Boulevard, Pico Rivera, CA 90660

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission receive and file this overview of the
CERT Program and discuss potential recruitment efforts.

FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Discussion on the Climate Adaptation Planning Grant Program

BACKGROUND

In 2020, the City of Artesia developed its inaugural Local Hazard Mitigation Plan (LHMP)
to analyze and mitigate natural hazard risks, which identified climate change, dam
inundation, earthquake hazards, and winter storms as key threats to the City. The plan
thoroughly evaluates these hazards, detailing their nature and potential effects, and
outlines 31 specific actions aimed at safeguarding both new and existing buildings and
infrastructure, thereby reducing overall risk and potential losses. The LHMP is required
to be updated every five years, part of the review process for an updated play includes if
any of the action item have been addressed in the previous five years.

The City is taking concrete steps towards addressing the identified climate risks. To this
end, the City is in the process of preparing a grant application for the Climate Adaptation
Planning program from the California Department of Transportation. The purpose of the
program is to aid local entities in identifying and assessing vulnerabilities, developing
adaptation strategies, and enhancing resilience against climate risks.

ANALYSIS
The City’s proposed project for the grant application includes several key components
aimed at bolstering Artesia’s resilience to climate change and taking action to address
hazards identified in the LHMP:

  •  Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment: A detailed analysis of Artesia’s
  susceptibility to climate change impacts, focusing on transportation infrastructure
  and community vulnerabilities.
  •  Climate Action and Adaptation Plans: The development of comprehensive plan
  to address identified vulnerabilities, focusing on both mitigation and adaptation
  strategies.
   ITEM 5

  •  Evacuation Analysis and Strategy Plan: Analyzing and planning efficient and
  safe evacuation routes and methods during extreme weather events.
  •  Planning for Extreme Weather Events: Developing plans to address various
  scenarios, such as flash flooding and heatwaves.

The Commission’s insights are crucial for developing a competitive and comprehensive
project proposal. Staff is requesting that the Commission discuss and provide direction in
the following areas:

  •  Community Engagement:
  o Strategies for effectively engaging underserved communities in project
  planning and implementation.
  o Recommendations for ensuring that the project addresses the specific
  safety needs of these communities.
  o A plan for engaging the community in understanding and participating in
  climate adaptation and evacuation strategies.
  •  Collaboration and Partnerships:
  o Suggestions for fostering collaboration and partnerships with local
  emergency services, law enforcement, and other relevant organizations.

Staff will incorporate the Commission's input into the City’s grant application and will
submit the application by the January 18, 2024 deadline. Grant awards are expected to
be announced in June 2024. If awarded, the Public Safety Commission will be asked to
provide feedback in the development of the items listed above prior to their approval by
City Council.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission provide direction on the City’s grant
application to the Climate Adaptation Planning Program from the California Department
of Transportation.
